title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
summary: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $λ$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(λ^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere.…
